subject: Hosted API commit tiers & marketplace billing — pricing impact
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API commit tiers & marketplace billing — initial proposal

Hi Sara,

Great to chat yesterday — appreciate the transparency on Acme's projected usage. Per our discussion, I've put together an initial pricing sketch for the Hosted API (usage-based per-token) with optional monthly commit tiers. The attached spreadsheet is the working proposal. High-level options: 

- No commit (pay-as-you-go): list rate $0.0008 / token, standard volume discounts apply at monthly thresholds.
- 3 month commit ($300k total): effective per-token ~ $0.0006 (approx 25% off list).
- 12 month commit ($3.6M annual): effective per-token ~ $0.0005 (approx 37.5% off list) + priority capacity.

Two important notes about billing: if you purchase via AWS Marketplace (Private Offer), we need to reflect marketplace fees in the list price. That typically means the headline discount we can offer on the Marketplace invoice is slightly reduced compared to direct billing because the marketplace takes a percentage on transactions. Practically, we can meet most of the effective economics you care about, but the structure will look different on the invoice and in procurement paperwork.

Can you confirm whether Acme prefers to contract directly with Redwood or must go through AWS Marketplace? If the latter I can loop in Karthik and our finance lead (Marissa) to work through a Private Offer/PO workflow and final numbers.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: RDW-Acme-pricing-proposal.xlsx (pricing workbook, assumptions sheet)

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-05-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers & marketplace billing — initial proposal

Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. Acme prefers to buy through AWS Marketplace where possible due to our internal procurement rules (single vendor, consolidated billing). We may be able to do direct for pilot spend, but for any enterprise commit we need Marketplace PO/contracting.

Two asks from procurement:
1) Can you provide the effective per-token after marketplace fees (we need to show our finance team the unit economics)?
2) For a 12-month commit, can you confirm whether the committed discount is guaranteed for the term or subject to cadence-based repricing?

Would be great to get a short note we can attach to our PO explaining the delta between direct and marketplace pricing.

Sara Jones
Head of Product, Acme Corp
Sara.Jones@acme.com

Date: 2026-05-16T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: looping in finance + marketplace — Acme (pricing mechanics)

Hi Sara, looping in Karthik (sales leader) and Marissa (finance) to clarify mechanics. Karthik/Marissa — Acme prefers Marketplace procurement for enterprise commit; Sara asked for effective per-token after marketplace fees and whether discounts are guaranteed for the 12-month term.

Sara — quick note from Karthik below (copying verbatim):

On 16 May 2026, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Marketplace implications are two-fold:
> 1) Marketplace (AWS) charges a platform fee on the transaction which we typically cover by setting a slightly higher list price on Marketplace offers. That means the invoice line item shows a higher unit price, but the Private Offer can be structured so the effective economics to Acme match the committed discount target.
> 2) Marketplace Private Offers add administrative steps (PO, AWS approval, subscription binding) that add ~3-10 business days to close.
>
> For a guaranteed 12-month commit, we can lock the discount for the contracted term in both direct and Private Offer structures — the difference is how the numbers are surfaced on the invoice. If Acme needs the numbers shown as a specific net-per-token on the invoice, we can reflect that in the Private Offer amount but it will include the marketplace margin.

Marissa will attach the price model with both direct and marketplace columns so you can see the end-to-end math.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers & marketplace billing — pricing impact (attachment)

Hi all,

Attached is a short workbook that shows: list price, proposed Redwood discount, AWS marketplace fee assumption (10%), and resulting net to Acme. Summary rows: 

- Direct billing (12m $3.6M commit): list $0.0008, Redwood discount 37.5% -> net $0.0005 / token.
- AWS Marketplace Private Offer equivalent: list (marketplace-facing) $0.00089, Redwood discount applied -> net on AWS invoice $0.00057 / token; after AWS fee pulled out, effective economics to Acme ≈ $0.00051.

What this means practically: we can structure a Private Offer so Acme's economics are within ~2% of direct billing. The invoice presentation and the PO flow differ, but the committed economics can be matched closely. The attached sheet also includes a column for alternative fee splits (if marketplace fee is negotiated down).

I've included a short note you can attach to the PO summarizing the delta. If Acme's procurement insists on an exact single-line net-per-token, we can commit to that number in the Private Offer but we'd ask that Acme acknowledge marketplace fee pass-through in the contract appendix.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: RDW-Acme-pricing-proposal.xlsx (version with marketplace column)

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>

Marissa — thanks, the workbook is helpful. A couple follow-ups before we escalate to legal/finance:

1) Can you confirm billing cadence (monthly invoices via AWS or consolidated annual invoice)?
2) If we commit and then materially exceed the committed consumption, is there an overage rate or automatic true-up?

If you can add a one-page note that procurement can attach to the PO describing the Private Offer mechanics (invoice flow, who receives credits, tax handling), that will get us to the internal approvals faster. Can we also schedule a 30-minute call with marketplace support included?

Sara

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers & marketplace billing — next steps

Sara, marketplace team —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers:
- Billing cadence: AWS issues monthly marketplace usage invoices that are charged to Acme; Redwood reconciles via our marketplace reporting and the Private Offer. For direct billing we issue monthly invoices to Acme's AP.
- Overages: we treat committed tiers as an annual/term guarantee. If monthly consumption exceeds the committed monthly run-rate, overages bill at a pre-agreed overage rate (we usually set overage at 110% of the committed per-token rate to discourage uncontrolled spikes). We can also structure a buffer (10% runway) if that's preferred.

Action items:
1) Marissa to produce a 1-page PO attachable note explaining Private Offer mechanics (attached PDF).
2) Marketplace team to confirm expected fee % and timeline for Private Offer onboarding; AWS, can you confirm?
3) Schedule 30-minute call: propose Thu 2026-05-20 11:00 AM PDT.

I'll prepare a draft Private Offer and send to Sara's procurement if we get AWS acknowledgement of fee/timeline.

Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
